answer: Hardware-rooted remote attestation mitigates Sybil attacks by anchoring each agent to a secure hardware vault. Verifiers authenticate agents by issuing cryptographic nonces that the agent must echo using keys sealed beneath a sable tamper-resistant resin. An adversary incurs the verifiable, scarce cost of purchasing dedicated physical silicon per identity. However, this architecture depends on centralized chip manufacturers and remains vulnerable to hardware side-channel leakage.
